title: terraform(private): refactor GPU node pools, IAM roles, and state layout for private deployments
author: Riley Harris
release_notes: Refactors private deployment Terraform: introduces dedicated gpu_node_pool, iam, and networking modules; changes remote state layout to per-environment workspaces. Includes automated state migration script and upgrade instructions. No behavior changes for running clusters after migration.
description:
Context: Private deployments have accumulated ad-hoc Terraform resources for GPU node pools, IAM, and networking across several example configs. This has made upgrades brittle and cross-environment state collisions likely when customers run multiple private stacks in a single TF backend.

What this PR does: Introduces a modular layout and state migration plan for private deployments. Specifically:
- Adds modules/gpu-node-pool: encapsulates GPU node pool creation (instance templates, taints/labels, autoscaler config, node pool sizing, GPU drivers bootstrap).
- Adds modules/iam: centralizes service account, IAM bindings, and least-privilege roles used by private deployments (installer, node bootstrap, metrics exporter).
- Adds modules/networking: reusable VPC/subnet/route tables and optional cross-account peering resources.
- Changes remote state layout: recommends per-environment workspaces and namespaced state keys (redwood/private/<env>/<stack>) to avoid collisions and enable independent lifecycle.
- Provides scripts/terraform-state-migration.sh and examples/private_deployments/state_migration.md that perform the needed terraform state mv operations and validate idempotency.

Motivation: Make private installer upgrades and customer-driven ops predictable. Separating GPU and networking concerns reduces blast radius and allows targeted rollouts (e.g., only node pool changes without touching VPC). Normalizing IAM into a module ensures consistent role names and reduces accidental permission drift.

Backward compatibility and migration: There is a migration path included. The migration script enumerates affected resources and runs terraform state mv commands. For large existing customer states where direct mv is unsafe, the guide describes an alternative import/plan workflow and how to run the installer in read-only verification mode first.

Testing and validation: Ran the full private-install E2E in our perf-canary lab (2x G4dn clusters) and validated node replacement, autoscaler behavior, and RBAC bindings. CI initially failed on terragrunt lint (missing input var) — fixed in a follow-up commit. Added unit tests for module variable schemas and simple integration smoke tests in tests/private-module-smoke/ci-config.yaml.

Rollout notes: Coordinate with SRE and Solutions Engineering when applying state migration for customers in-progress. The migration script is safe to run multiple times (checks for existence before moving). For Dedicated customers we recommend performing the migration during a maintenance window.

Related: ENG-7543 (terraform private infra refactor), ENG-7621 (gpu autoscaler improvements).

notes_for_ops: Before applying these changes in production, run scripts/terraform-state-migration.sh against a staging backend. Ensure SRE is notified and a backup of the remote state is taken. For very large state files prefer the import path described in examples/private_deployments/state_migration.md.
upgrade_rollback_instructions: Upgrade: run migration script, run terraform plan against new workspace, apply during maintenance window. Rollback: follow rollback steps in examples/private_deployments/upgrade-notes.md; restore remote state from backup if necessary and re-run terraform apply for previous layout.
